title: CmdPal: Some UI messages handled by MainWindow are not marshaled to the dispatcher thread
author: jiripolasek
summary: Command Palette's MainWindow receives messenger notifications with inconsistent UI-thread dispatching: some receivers enqueue UI work, while window-show receivers directly mutate window state.

status.label: Design ready
status.detail: A focused dispatcher-boundary change is ready for maintainer approval; ordering and foreground behavior need targeted validation.

next_action: Approve the dispatcher-boundary design, then validate notification ordering and window activation from a non-UI sender.

judgment.rationale: The reported source inspection identifies direct UI/window mutations in MainWindow message receivers even though the same class explicitly dispatches other potentially background-thread notifications. WeakReferenceMessenger delivery retains the sender's thread, so receivers that touch WinUI or HWND state need one consistent UI-thread boundary.
evidence: The issue is open, has no comments, no linked closing PR, and is labeled Issue-Bug and Product-Command Palette.
The reporter is assigned to the issue, and the issue body identifies MainWindow handlers that are and are not marshaled to the UI thread.
MainWindow.Receive(HideWindowMessage), Receive(QuitMessage), Receive(ExpandCompactModeMessage), and Receive(MaximizeForDialogMessage) use DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue before changing UI/window state.
MainWindow.Receive(ShowWindowMessage) directly resets session state and calls ShowHwnd, and Receive(ShowPaletteAtMessage) directly restores window position and calls ShowHwnd.
MainWindow registers all of these receivers with WeakReferenceMessenger.Default, which does not introduce thread marshaling.
Program.OnActivated documents that activation handling must remain synchronous so the sending instance does not exit before its arguments are processed.
No public PR search result references #50388; no duplicate or existing public fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused MainWindow dispatcher-boundary fix that preserves the synchronous activation path, then validate each non-UI notification source and window-show ordering.

fix_assessment.rationale: There is no public fix attempt for this issue. The receiver implementations expose a narrow, locally owned thread-affinity defect, but queued delivery can change activation/show ordering and needs a focused runtime check.

proposed_fixes.title: Make MainWindow messenger UI mutations consistently dispatcher-bound
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MainWindow is registered as a recipient for messages that can be sent by non-UI work, but its show and several state-mutating receivers execute directly. This contrasts with existing receivers that explicitly enqueue UI/window work and risks accessing WinUI/HWND state from the sender's thread.
plan: Inventory every MainWindow IRecipient<T>.Receive implementation and classify whether it mutates WinUI state, HWND state, or shared session state consumed by UI code.

Extract private UI-thread handlers for window show, dock-position show, session-counter updates, developer-ribbon toggling, drag state, and HWND access where appropriate; make the public messenger receivers enqueue only the UI-affine work.
Keep Program.OnActivated and MainWindow.HandleLaunchNonUI on their existing synchronous activation contract; do not replace activation completion with fire-and-forget dispatch.
For messages with observable ordering requirements, use a completion mechanism or a sender-side UI scheduler rather than assuming TryEnqueue preserves synchronous behavior.
Add focused coverage or test seams around the dispatcher boundary and manually exercise summon, dock-to-palette transition, dismissal, drag completion, and activation redirection.
verification: Build the Command Palette UI project in the repository's supported Visual Studio configuration.

From a non-UI sender or dispatcher test seam, deliver ShowWindowMessage, ShowPaletteAtMessage, HideWindowMessage, and QuitMessage; confirm all UI/HWND operations execute on MainWindow.DispatcherQueue.

Launch a second Command Palette instance with an activation payload and confirm Program.OnActivated still completes synchronously, the payload is processed once, and the sender can exit without losing it.
Manually summon Command Palette, open it from a Dock item, drag a list item, dismiss it, and repeat the sequence while checking that foreground and visibility behavior remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The inconsistent receiver implementations and thread-affinity risk are directly visible in the current code. The exact sender-thread combinations and ordering constraints for every message need a focused runtime trace before selecting whether each receiver can safely use asynchronous queueing.

issue_context.summary: A Command Palette maintainer reported that MainWindow handles related messenger notifications inconsistently: some handlers marshal to the dispatcher and others access window state immediately.
known_information: The report targets a Command Palette development build from Visual Studio on the main branch.
The report contains a source screenshot and names the inconsistent MainWindow message handling rather than an end-user symptom.
The issue has no discussion comments, linked closing pull requests, or duplicate references.
The issue is assigned to reporter jiripolasek and has the Product-Command Palette label.
MainWindow registers the affected messages with WeakReferenceMessenger.Default.
Current handlers for HideWindowMessage and QuitMessage explicitly enqueue before touching the window, while ShowWindowMessage and ShowPaletteAtMessage directly call ShowHwnd.
inferences: Because messenger delivery occurs on the sending thread, direct handlers may access MainWindow state off the UI thread when a future or existing sender is background-threaded.
A blanket fire-and-forget conversion could regress activation delivery because the activation path documents a synchronous completion requirement.
The assigned Command Palette maintainer is the appropriate public ownership signal, but assignment alone is not evidence of an existing implementation.
issue_context.analysis: The source establishes a concrete consistency and correctness gap without requiring generic diagnostics. The implementation should centralize the UI-thread boundary, while preserving the synchronous activation flow and proving that queueing does not reorder visibility, focus, or payload processing.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue body, labels, assignee, empty discussion, timeline, and closed-by pull-request references.
Searched public PowerToys pull requests and issues for #50388 and dispatcher-thread references; no linked duplicate or fix attempt was found.
Inspected src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/MainWindow.xaml.cs and compared direct receiver implementations with receivers that call DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue.

Inspected src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Program.cs and App.xaml.cs; activation and app setup establish the UI synchronization context, and Program documents the synchronous activation constraint.

Reviewed recent MainWindow history, including CmdPal UI-thread backdrop work in PR #49755 and current Command Palette changes. The issue's assignee is also the recent author of Command Palette MainWindow changes.

information_gaps.information: For each affected message, the actual sender and whether it can run off the MainWindow DispatcherQueue, plus any required synchronous completion or ordering guarantee.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines which receivers may safely enqueue and which need a synchronous dispatcher handoff or a sender-side scheduling change, avoiding lost activation data or changed focus/visibility ordering.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Capture a focused debugger trace or add temporary thread-id logging while exercising secondary-instance activation, normal summon, Dock-to-palette show, hide/dismiss, and drag completion; report the message type, sender, and UI-thread status.

design.root_cause: MainWindow mixes direct WeakReferenceMessenger receiver execution with DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue-based execution. Direct receivers such as Receive(ShowWindowMessage) and Receive(ShowPaletteAtMessage) mutate MainWindow/session/window state on the sender thread, while nearby receivers acknowledge that their messages can arrive off the UI thread. The issue is a missing consistent thread-affinity boundary, not a confirmed failure in every sender path.
evidence: MainWindow registers all affected messages with WeakReferenceMessenger.Default in its constructor.
Receive(HideWindowMessage) and Receive(QuitMessage) explicitly marshal window operations through DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue.
Receive(ShowWindowMessage) resets MainWindow fields and calls ShowHwnd directly; Receive(ShowPaletteAtMessage) restores window position and calls ShowHwnd directly.
Program.OnActivated states that handling must be synchronous so redirected activation arguments are not lost when the sending process exits.
The issue body precisely identifies the inconsistent dispatch pattern, and public issue/PR search found no existing fix.

affected_files.purpose: Owns the Command Palette HWND, messenger registrations, show/hide behavior, and affected IRecipient<T>.Receive implementations.
Routes redirected activation to the existing Command Palette instance and defines the synchronous completion constraint.
Creates MainWindow on the UI thread and hands initial activation to it.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The public messenger receivers mutate session/window-position fields and invoke ShowHwnd directly on the message sender's thread.
implementation_steps.change: Separate message receipt from UI work. Route UI-affine show work through MainWindow.DispatcherQueue, retaining private handlers that perform the existing field updates and ShowHwnd call together on the UI thread.
edge_cases: Do not split session initialization and ShowHwnd across separate queue entries.
Confirm queue rejection during shutdown is handled consistently with existing Hide/Quit behavior.
Preserve docking coordinates and anchors as immutable message data until the UI handler executes.
tests: Use a dispatcher test seam or non-UI sender to assert that show work runs on MainWindow.DispatcherQueue.
Manually validate normal summon and Dock-to-palette show behavior.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Several related receivers directly update session counters, visual state, drag state, or return the HWND; only some of the class's receiver methods marshal explicitly.
implementation_steps.change: Classify these receivers by thread affinity and enforce it uniformly. Queue UI/HWND access, protect or confine session counters to the UI thread, and retain direct execution only where the sender is contractually UI-thread-bound and that contract is documented and tested.
edge_cases: Do not turn a request/response message such as GetHwndMessage into an asynchronous response without changing its sender contract.
Do not enqueue drag completion twice; its delayed foreground handoff already queues StealForeground.
Avoid unsynchronized counter mutations while EndSession reads and resets session telemetry.
tests: Exercise hide/dismiss, drag-complete foreground recovery, telemetry counters, developer ribbon, and HWND request paths from the documented sender contexts.
Add a regression test for any receiver whose sender can be intentionally invoked from a background task.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: OnActivated invokes MainWindow.HandleLaunchNonUI synchronously because the redirecting process remains blocked until activation is fully handled.
implementation_steps.change: Keep that call synchronous. If its downstream work needs the UI dispatcher, provide a synchronous completion handshake or make the activation sender enter the UI scheduler before returning; do not use an unobserved TryEnqueue for payload processing.
edge_cases: A secondary instance may exit immediately after OnActivated returns.
Timeout and shutdown paths must not leave a redirected activation waiting indefinitely.
Initial launch from App.OnLaunched already occurs on the UI thread and must remain behaviorally unchanged.
tests: Launch a second instance with an activation argument and assert the existing instance handles it exactly once before the sender exits.
Repeat while Command Palette is hidden and while a Dock window initiates showing the palette.

verify: Build src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.csproj in the repository's supported Visual Studio configuration.
Run the existing Command Palette UI/ViewModels tests that cover the touched behavior, adding targeted dispatcher-boundary tests where the project has an appropriate test seam.
Manually test normal summon, Dock invocation, secondary-instance activation, hide/dismiss, drag completion, and shutdown with a debugger or focused trace confirming UI-thread execution.
Confirm that no activation payload, visibility update, focus transition, or session telemetry record is lost or reordered.
risks: Asynchronous dispatch can reorder work that was previously synchronous, especially redirected activation and request/response messages.
Changing thread ownership of telemetry/session fields can introduce races with EndSession.
A broad mechanical conversion could affect handlers whose senders are already UI-thread-bound without improving correctness.
alternatives: Leave direct receivers unchanged and rely on current senders remaining UI-thread-bound: rejected because the class already documents background delivery for related messages and messenger delivery does not marshal threads.
Queue every receiver blindly: rejected because synchronous activation and request/response behavior may require completion before return.
Replace WeakReferenceMessenger globally: rejected because the defect is localized to MainWindow's UI-affinity boundary and a global rewrite would expand risk.

actions.label: Request affected-message thread and ordering trace

comment.body: Thanks for identifying the inconsistent `MainWindow` dispatcher handling. The direct receivers are a clear thread-affinity concern, but the right handoff depends on whether each sender requires synchronous completion. Could you capture a focused debugger trace (or temporary thread-id logging) for secondary-instance activation, normal summon, Dock-to-palette show, hide/dismiss, and drag completion? For each affected message, please include the sender, whether it is on `MainWindow.DispatcherQueue`, and any ordering requirement. That will distinguish handlers that can safely enqueue from activation or request/response paths that need a synchronous handoff.
